task.title: SUPPORTORDERS
task.spec:
You are working in a checkout of shopizer, a Java e-commerce platform (Maven, several modules; JDK 21 is installed and JAVA_HOME is set).

Our support team works from the admin order screens and keeps hitting problems:

- When a customer asks us to delete their account (DELETE /api/v1/private/customer/{id}), we can't open their orders afterwards: GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id} gives HTTP 404, and looking up the orders they placed (GET /api/v1/private/orders/customers/{id}) gives HTTP 404 too. We have to keep orders, and answer questions about them, for years after an account is closed.
- The order list (GET /api/v1/private/orders) only ever shows its first page. Asking for any later page returns no orders and a total of 0, so older orders can't be found by browsing.

Fix the order screens:

- An order whose customer account was deleted opens exactly as before (GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id}), with the billing and delivery details and the email it was placed with; it just has no customer. Its status can still be changed, and its history and payment transactions read, as for any order.
- GET /api/v1/private/orders/customers/{id} lists every order placed by that customer id, newest first, whether or not the account still exists, with "recordsTotal" the number of those orders. An id with no orders gives an empty list with "recordsTotal" 0.
- GET /api/v1/private/orders?count={n}&page={p} returns page p (the first page is 0) of the orders matching the request's filters (status, email, name, id), newest first, with "recordsTotal" the number of matching orders and "totalPages" the number of pages of n. A page after the last has no orders but the same totals.
- Registering again with a deleted customer's email creates a new, separate account, which sees none of the old account's orders.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.

runs.report:
## Scope and evidence

The task targets this repository’s Shopizer backend. No GitHub issue or prior implementation was supplied; the checkout contains only the existing baseline commit and no relevant local changes.

Confirmed code paths:

- `sm-shop/.../api/v1/order/OrderApi.java:112-152` returns 404 when the customer no longer exists, even though orders retain `customerId`.
- `OrderFacadeImpl.java:923-931` builds customer-order criteria from `customerId`, but the API currently requires a live `Customer` first.
- `sm-core-model/.../order/Order.java:69-71,166` explicitly documents detached customers and stores the order’s customer ID and placed email independently.
- `OrderFacadeImpl.java:1107-1125` already treats a missing customer as allowed for single-order reads; `ReadableOrderPopulator.java:87-105` obtains billing email and address snapshots from the order.
- `CustomerServiceImpl.java:100-111` deletes the customer record and attributes but does not delete orders.
- `sm-core/.../repositories/order/OrderRepositoryImpl.java:138-260` implements admin filtering, descending ID ordering, count queries, and pagination.
- `RepositoryHelper.java:29-35` uses zero-based page offsets but calculates pages as `count / pageSize + 1`, which is wrong for exact multiples and zero-count handling. `OrderFacadeImpl.java:947-950` replaces an empty page with `recordsTotal: 0`, losing the matching total for out-of-range pages.
- `OrderFacadeImpl.java:961-964` maps totals only when the page has orders. The repository’s fetched order data is suitable for the existing admin detail, status, history, and payment flows.
- `Customer.java` has a uniqueness constraint only on merchant plus customer nickname, not email (`Customer.java:54-55`); registration checks the username/nick, so a deleted account’s email can be reused unless another path imposes a restriction.

## Problem and likely implementation scope

1. Change `/private/orders/customers/{id}` to query orders directly by persisted customer ID, without requiring the customer row. Populate each result’s customer only when the account still exists; deleted-account results must retain order billing/delivery/email snapshots and have no customer object. Return an empty list with `recordsTotal: 0` for an ID with no orders.
2. Correct admin order-list pagination and response mapping. Preserve all request filters (status, email, name, ID), descending newest-first ordering, zero-based pages, matching `recordsTotal`, and mathematically correct `totalPages`. Empty or out-of-range pages must retain the count and page total.
3. Verify registration after deletion uses the normal new-customer path and does not associate the new account with historical orders; order ownership must remain keyed by the new customer ID, not email.

Likely affected components are `OrderApi`, `OrderFacade`/`OrderFacadeImpl`, `OrderRepositoryImpl`/pagination helper, and focused order/customer integration or service tests. Existing `OrderApiIntegrationTest` is ignored and currently contains no assertions, so new executable coverage will likely be needed. Existing `OrderTest` covers only a basic service listing path.

## Acceptance checks for Implement

- Create an account and order, delete the account, then GET `/api/v1/private/orders/{orderId}` returns 200 with the same order ID, billing and delivery details, placed email, status, history, and payment transactions; customer is absent/null.
- After deletion, GET `/api/v1/private/orders/customers/{deletedId}` returns 200, includes every matching order newest first, and reports the number of matching orders in `recordsTotal`.
- GET `/api/v1/private/orders/customers/{id}` for an ID with no orders returns 200 with an empty orders collection and `recordsTotal: 0`.
- Admin status update and history/payment reads continue to work for the orphaned order.
- With more than one page of orders, `count=n&page=0,1,...` returns the corresponding newest-first slices; filters for status, email, name, and ID affect both results and totals.
- A page after the last returns no orders while preserving the same `recordsTotal` and `totalPages`; exact multiples of `count` produce no extra page.
- Re-registering with the deleted customer’s email creates a distinct customer ID, and that account’s order lookup returns none of the deleted account’s historical orders.

## Assumptions and decisions

- “Newest first” follows the repository’s established `order by o.id desc`; if business data requires purchase-date ordering, that would be a consequential behavior change requiring approval.
- Existing API response field names and order DTO shape should remain unchanged.
- No explicit design approval is needed: this is a focused bug fix with clear acceptance checks and established repository conventions. Complexity is medium because it spans API, facade, repository pagination, and regression coverage.
runs.summary: Traced the order APIs, persistence, deletion, and pagination paths; confirmed the requested work belongs to this repository and identified the existing defects and test coverage needed for Implement.
